reactionOptions.text: Fund a dedicated legal aid cell to assist farmers in drafting and submitting affidavits to the court.

risk.badOutcome: Court hearings drag on for months, testing the patience of displaced farmers.

reactionOptions.text: Propose a panel of retired judges to mediate between the Tata management and the Krishi Jami Raksha Committee.

risk.badOutcome: Both the government and radical farm leaders reject mediation, insisting on their legal positions.

title: Singur Fencing Drive Triggers Violent Clashes With Police
description: The state administration deploys thousands of police personnel to fence off the acquired land in Singur. Protesters attempt to breach the barricades, leading to tear gas firing and a lathi charge. Several farmers and police officers are injured.

reactionOptions.text: Organise a 24-hour statewide general strike (bandh) to protest the police action in Singur.

risk.badOutcome: Strikes cause loss of daily wages for informal workers, leading to mixed public reactions.

risk.badOutcome: The probe is delayed, and its terms of reference are criticized as weak.

title: Durga Puja Coordination Committee Resolves Political Bookstall Dispute
description: During the annual Durga Puja festival, local committees clash over the placement of political bookstalls near major puja pandals. The opposition accuses municipal officials of selectively denying permits to anti-government groups.

risk.badOutcome: Local cadres defy the directive, leading to minor scuffles at select pandals.

reactionOptions.text: Distribute free booklets detailing the Singur land struggle at all available community spaces.

risk.badOutcome: Voters seek holiday entertainment and ignore heavy political literature.

risk.badOutcome: Organizers find political sponsorship too valuable to restrict.

title: Opposition Leader Detained At Singur Border, Spontaneous Protests Erupt
description: Police detain opposition leader Mamata Banerjee on the Durgapur Expressway as she attempts to enter Singur to address a farmers' rally. The detention sparks spontaneous road blockades and protests in Kolkata and major district towns.

reactionOptions.text: Launch statewide rallies and sit-ins at administrative offices to protest the high-handedness of the police.

title: Mamata Starts Hunger Strike; Nandigram Chemical Hub SEZ Notice Issued
description: Mamata Banerjee begins an indefinite hunger strike in Kolkata against the Singur acquisition. Meanwhile, the Haldia Development Authority issues a notice planning a chemical hub/Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Nandigram, East Midnapore, sparking local panic.

reactionOptions.text: Send organisers to Nandigram to hold village meetings and prepare local committees against the chemical hub.

risk.badOutcome: Report is dismissed by industrial planners as exaggerated and anti-modern.

title: Nandigram Cut Off By Roadblocks As Villagers Resist SEZ Notice
description: Following the chemical hub SEZ notice, the newly formed Bhumi Uchhed Pratirodh Committee (BUPC) cuts off access to Nandigram in East Midnapore. Road bridges are demolished and deep trenches are dug to prevent police vehicles and ruling party organizers from entering.

risk.badOutcome: Cadres of the ruling party attempt to break the roadblocks, leading to clashes.

reactionOptions.text: Call on the district administration to organize peace talks involving all stakeholders, including the BUPC, in a neutral venue.

risk.badOutcome: Radicalized villagers reject talks, demanding the withdrawal of all police cases first.

reactionOptions.text: No comment.

title: Bomb Blast At Kamakhyaguri Railway Station In North Bengal

risk.badOutcome: Statement is dismissed as vague political rhetoric by local hill groups.

title: Nandigram Police Firing: Fourteen Killed As Police Attempt Entrance
description: In a major operation to dismantle BUPC roadblocks and restore administration, state police enter Nandigram. A confrontation leads to police firing, resulting in the deaths of 14 villagers. The incident triggers massive outrage across the state.

reactionOptions.text: Condemn the firing and send a non-political delegation of artists and writers to document the ground reality.

risk.badOutcome: Delegation is blocked at the border by local cadres, highlighting state-level polarization.

reactionOptions.text: No comment.

title: Siliguri Transport Strike Over Local Development Grievances
description: A transport workers' union launches an indefinite strike in Siliguri, the gateway to North Bengal, protesting poor road conditions and local municipal tax hikes. Cargo movement to Darjeeling and Sikkim is severely disrupted.

reactionOptions.text: Suspend the municipal tax hikes temporarily and release state road repair grants for North Bengal highways.

risk.badOutcome: Municipal bodies face budget shortages, delaying essential civic works.

reactionOptions.text: Address rallies at Siliguri bus terminals and demand direct central intervention to resolve the impasse.

risk.badOutcome: Extended strike causes food inflation in Darjeeling hills, turning hill voters against the strike.

risk.badOutcome: Arbitration board takes months, and transport operators refuse to end the strike during hearings.

title: Intellectuals And Artists Lead Massive Silent March In Kolkata Against Nandigram
description: Prominent Bengali intellectuals, writers, and film directors lead a silent march of over fifty thousand citizens in Kolkata. They protest the Nandigram firing and the government's cultural response, signaling a major shift in the state's traditional support base.

reactionOptions.text: Invite prominent march leaders to join a state cultural advisory committee to address public concerns.

reactionOptions.text: Propose constructing state-backed cultural hubs and art galleries in district towns to decentralize cultural spending.

title: Tata Nano Factory Construction Proceeds Under Heavy Police Security
description: Inside the fenced area at Singur, construction of the main plant building proceeds. Outside, police maintain roadblocks, occasionally dispersing small groups of farmers attempting to block trucks carrying raw materials.

title: Midday Meal Supply Quality Scandal Exposed In Birbhum Schools
description: Media reports document sub-standard food grains and insect-infested lentils supplied to midday meals in Birbhum schools. Parents protest, alleging local politicians and suppliers are pocketing government welfare funds.

risk.badOutcome: Government suppliers go on strike, disrupting midday meals for thousands of children for weeks.

title: Teesta River Embankment Breach Submerges Jalpaiguri Villages
description: A sudden breach in the Teesta River embankment following heavy monsoon rains floods over twenty villages in Jalpaiguri district. Local residents complain that repair requests submitted to the irrigation department were ignored for months.

reactionOptions.text: Deploy disaster response teams and release emergency funds to construct a temporary ring embankment.

title: Suspicious Death of Rizwanur Rahman Sparks Massive Public Anger
description: A computer graphics teacher, Rizwanur Rahman, is found dead near railway tracks in Kolkata. The death follows his marriage to Priyanka Todi, daughter of a wealthy industrialist. Public anger erupts as allegations surface that senior Kolkata Police officers harassed the couple on behalf of the family.

reactionOptions.text: Order the immediate transfer of the implicated police officers and transfer the case to the CID for investigation.

reactionOptions.text: Lead peaceful candlelight marches in Kolkata demanding a CBI investigation and the resignation of the police commissioner.

risk.badOutcome: Some protest marches lead to minor clashes with police, resulting in road closures.

title: Kolkata Police Commissioner Transferred After Sustained Protests
description: Following weeks of public protests over the Rizwanur Rahman case, the state government transfers the Kolkata Police Commissioner and two deputy commissioners. The CBI registers a case to investigate the circumstances of the death.

reactionOptions.text: Instruct all state departments to cooperate fully with the CBI investigation to ensure justice.

risk.badOutcome: CBI questioning of senior political advisors raises fresh corruption concerns.

reactionOptions.text: Demand a complete restructuring of the police administration to prevent political interference in civilian life.

title: Nandigram Recaptured; Taslima Nasreen Protests Trigger Kolkata Riots
description: Ruling party cadres forcibly re-enter and 'recapture' Nandigram after months of roadblocks. Meanwhile, in Kolkata, violent protests demanding the eviction of writer Taslima Nasreen lead to street clashes, forcing the government to deploy the Army.

title: High Court Declares Nandigram Firing Illegal, Orders Compensation
description: The Kolkata High Court declares the police firing of March 14, 2007, illegal and unjustified. The court directs the state government to pay immediate compensation to the families of those killed and injured, delivering a blow to the administration.

title: Bird Flu Outbreak In Birbhum Triggers Statewide Poultry Culling
description: A confirmed outbreak of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza (bird flu) in Birbhum district spreads to adjacent districts. The animal resources department deploys teams to cull lakhs of poultry, promising compensation to small farmers.

title: Trial Machinery Arrives At Singur Plant Amid Renewed Protests

description: Several tea gardens in the Dooars region of North Bengal declare lockouts following wage disputes and low export demands. Thousands of tribal plantation workers face loss of livelihood, with reports of malnutrition and food shortages in closed estates.

description: Led by Ruling Party, the opposition alliance launches an indefinite blockade at the Singur factory gates, camping on the national highway. They vow to prevent any factory operations until the 400 acres of land are returned to farmers.

description: Citing constant blockades and threats to its employees, Tata Motors suspends all construction work at the Singur plant. Chairman Ratan Tata warns that if the hostile political environment continues, the company will relocate the factory.

description: Tata Motors officially pulls out of Singur, moving the Nano project to Sanand, Gujarat. Meanwhile, a landmine blast targeting Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's convoy near Shalboni (West Midnapore) misses the vehicles but triggers security alarms.

description: Protesting alleged police harassment of tribal families following the Shalboni landmine blast, tribal villagers in Lalgarh launch an uprising under the PCPA banner. They dig up roads, remove police camps, and cut off the area from administration.

title: Diego Maradona's Historic Visit Sparks Celebration In Kolkata
description: International football icon Diego Maradona visits Kolkata. He is welcomed by massive crowds, inaugurates a youth football academy, and meets veteran political leaders, offering a brief period of celebration amid political controversies.

title: Netai Firing Fallout Roils Pre-Poll Bengal (2011-01)
description: Villagers in Netai, West Midnapore, continue protests after armed men allegedly linked to a CPI(M) harmadar camp opened fire on unarmed demonstrators, killing several. The incident becomes a rallying point for the opposition just months before the assembly election.

reactionOptions.text: The our coalition government orders a judicial probe into the firing and suspends the local police officer-in-charge.

risk.badOutcome: The probe is dismissed as a whitewash after the CBI later contradicts the state's findings.

reactionOptions.text: Lead a high-level party delegation to Netai and demands the immediate arrest of the rival cadres named by survivors.

risk.badOutcome: Local CPI(M) workers accuse the our party of exploiting grieving families for votes.

reactionOptions.text: The Election Commission convenes an all-party peace meeting in Midnapore to prevent further poll-season bloodshed.

risk.badOutcome: Hardliners on both sides skip the meeting, and it produces no binding commitments.

reactionOptions.text: The state home department declines to issue any statement on the Netai incident.

title: Police Fire on GJM Padyatra Near Jalpaiguri (2011-02)
description: Police open fire on Gorkha Janmukti Morcha activists marching from Gorubathan to Jaigaon, killing three, as the party presses its Gorkhaland statehood demand ahead of the state polls. The killings harden hill sentiment against Kolkata's rule.

reactionOptions.text: The our coalition government orders a magisterial inquiry and offers compensation to the victims' families.

risk.badOutcome: GJM rejects the inquiry as toothless and calls it too little, too late.

reactionOptions.text: GJM leader Bimal Gurung calls an indefinite hill bandh and demands the police officers involved be booked for murder.

risk.badOutcome: The bandh cripples tourism and tea exports, drawing criticism even from sympathetic hill residents.

reactionOptions.text: State and central officials agree to fast-track long-stalled Gorkhaland Territorial Administration talks to defuse hill anger.

risk.badOutcome: Rival Gorkha factions boycott the talks, questioning GJM's sole claim to represent the hills.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment on the firing beyond confirming three deaths.

title: EC Announces Six-Phase Poll Schedule as TMC-Congress Seal Seat Pact (2011-03)
description: The Election Commission schedules West Bengal's assembly polls across six phases from April 18, and the TMC finalises a seat-sharing arrangement with the Congress, formalising the anti-Left alliance behind Mamata Banerjee's 'Paribartan' campaign.

reactionOptions.text: The our coalition unveils its own manifesto early, betting on its record of land reform and industrial push in Singur-era Bengal.

risk.badOutcome: Younger rival cadres grumble that the manifesto ignores the Nandigram-Singur backlash.

reactionOptions.text: Our party leadership tours all six phases' constituencies, branding the vote a referendum on ending '34 years of misrule'.

risk.badOutcome: Opposition workers in some seats resent our party dictating terms of the seat-sharing formula.

reactionOptions.text: Agree to an Election Commission-brokered code of conduct pledge to curb booth-level violence during the six phases.

risk.badOutcome: Local-level clashes break out within days, undercutting the pledge's credibility.

reactionOptions.text: Our headquarters declines to react to the opposition alliance, calling it 'not worth dignifying'.

title: First Phase of Assembly Polling Opens in Naxalbari Belt (2011-04)
description: Voting begins in the jungle and tea-garden constituencies of the north, with record turnout reported despite a heavy security deployment against possible Maoist disruption. The high-stakes contest pits three decades of Left rule against Mamata Banerjee's challenge.

reactionOptions.text: Deploy additional central forces in Maoist-affected booths and extends voting hours in flood-prone char areas.

risk.badOutcome: Reports surface of booth capturing attempts in a few Jalpaiguri constituencies.

reactionOptions.text: Our poll agents demand re-polling at booths where they allege rival cadres intimidated voters.

risk.badOutcome: The Election Commission rejects most re-polling demands for lack of evidence.

reactionOptions.text: The Chief Electoral Officer holds an all-party briefing to coordinate complaint redressal across the remaining five phases.

risk.badOutcome: Some local leaders skip the briefing, calling it a formality.

reactionOptions.text: The opposition state unit offers no comment on turnout figures until later phases are complete.

title: TMC-Led Alliance Sweeps Polls, Mamata Banerjee Sworn In as CM (2011-05)
description: The Trinamool Congress-led alliance wins 227 of 294 seats, ending the Left Front's 34-year rule; Mamata Banerjee is sworn in as West Bengal's first woman chief minister on 20 May. Even outgoing CM Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee loses his own Jadavpur seat.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee immediately convenes her first cabinet meeting at Writers' Building and promises 'paribartan' will reach every village within a year.

risk.badOutcome: Bureaucrats used to three decades of Left administrative culture resist the pace of change.

reactionOptions.text: The opposition state secretary The party leadership concedes defeat but vows the party will rebuild from the grassroots and hold the new government to account.

risk.badOutcome: Cadre morale collapses in several districts, with reports of local leaders quietly switching sides.

reactionOptions.text: Outgoing and incoming administrations agree to a smooth transition briefing on finances and ongoing law-and-order cases.

risk.badOutcome: The handover briefing later becomes a point of dispute over the true state of the treasury.

reactionOptions.text: The outgoing our coalition cabinet declines further comment beyond a terse note thanking voters for 34 years of support.

title: Cabinet Orders Return of Singur Land to 'Unwilling' Farmers (2011-06)
description: In one of her first major decisions, Mamata Banerjee's cabinet orders 400 acres of the Tata Nano plant site at Singur returned to farmers who never accepted compensation, honouring the central promise of her election campaign.

reactionOptions.text: Fast-track the Singur Land Rehabilitation and Development Bill to enable the land transfer.

risk.badOutcome: Tata Motors signals it may challenge the land seizure in court, threatening the state's industrial credibility.

reactionOptions.text: Opposition leaders warn the move will scare away investors and accuse the government of reversing industrialisation for populism.

risk.badOutcome: The criticism is drowned out by widespread public celebration among Singur's farming families.

reactionOptions.text: An all-party legislative committee is formed to draft compensation terms acceptable to both willing and unwilling farmers.

risk.badOutcome: Disagreement over compensation formulas stalls the committee's work for weeks.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment on the cabinet's decision pending legal advice.

title: Tripartite Deal Creates Gorkhaland Territorial Administration (2011-07)
description: At Pintail Village near Siliguri, the Union Home Ministry, the West Bengal government and the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha sign a memorandum creating the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration, granting the hills a semi-autonomous council in place of statehood.

reactionOptions.text: Chief Minister Banerjee personally attends the Pintail Village signing, calling GTA proof that dialogue can replace decades of hill unrest.

risk.badOutcome: Rival Gorkha outfits like the GNLF denounce the deal as a sellout of the statehood demand.

reactionOptions.text: GJM general secretary Roshan Giri hails the agreement but insists it is only a stepping stone toward full Gorkhaland statehood.

risk.badOutcome: Hardline GJM cadres accuse Giri of settling for too little too soon.

reactionOptions.text: Union Home Minister Chidambaram, the state government and GJM jointly commit to a follow-up mechanism to resolve Dooars and Terai boundary disputes.

risk.badOutcome: The boundary follow-up mechanism stalls almost immediately over which mouzas to include.

reactionOptions.text: The Gorkha National Liberation Front refuses to engage with questions about the new administration it was excluded from.

title: Exhumed Keshpur Skeletons Implicate CPI(M) Veteran Susanta Ghosh (2011-08)
description: Police exhume skeletal remains linked to seven Trinamool workers who disappeared from Keshpur in 2002, reopening a case that names former Left Front minister Susanta Ghosh. The probe becomes an early test of how the new government treats its predecessors.

reactionOptions.text: The state police reopen the 2002 Keshpur disappearance case and question The former minister over his alleged role.

risk.badOutcome: CPI(M) accuses the government of selectively reviving a nine-year-old case only against its own leaders.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) calls the exhumation a politically motivated 'witch hunt' timed to humiliate a defeated party.

risk.badOutcome: The party's defence of Ghosh draws accusations that it is shielding a known hardliner.

reactionOptions.text: The Calcutta High Court is petitioned to independently monitor the investigation to insulate it from political pressure.

risk.badOutcome: Court proceedings drag on for years without a swift resolution.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment, referring all questions to his defence counsel.

title: New Government Releases White Paper on Bengal's Dire Finances (2011-09)
description: The Trinamool-led state government publishes a white paper detailing a debt burden it says was inherited from the Left Front, citing mounting interest payments that crowd out development spending. The document frames the new administration's fiscal narrative.

reactionOptions.text: Finance minister Amit Mitra appeals to the Centre for a debt restructuring package, citing the white paper's findings.

risk.badOutcome: The Centre is slow to respond, leaving the state's fiscal appeal in limbo for months.

reactionOptions.text: Reject the white paper's figures as selectively presented to blame the Left for the state's structural revenue problems.

risk.badOutcome: Independent economists partly corroborate the government's debt figures, undercutting the rebuttal.

reactionOptions.text: An all-party assembly panel is set up to review the state's debt servicing options together.

risk.badOutcome: The panel's recommendations are largely ignored once released.

reactionOptions.text: The state finance department declines to take further questions on the white paper's methodology.

title: GJM Signs 18-Point Mongpong Pact Proposing GATA (2011-10)
description: The Gorkha Janmukti Morcha and Adivasi groups sign an 18-point agreement at Mongpong proposing a new Gorkhaland and Adivasi Territorial Administration to fold in Dooars and Terai mouzas, complicating the freshly signed GTA framework.

reactionOptions.text: Appoint the Justice Shyamal Sen committee to examine which Dooars and Terai mouzas can be included.

risk.badOutcome: Adivasi groups accuse the committee of moving too slowly on their inclusion demands.

reactionOptions.text: GJM leaders press for all 398 mouzas they claim, threatening renewed agitation if the committee dilutes the demand.

risk.badOutcome: Non-Gorkha residents in the Dooars organise counter-protests against being folded into GATA.

reactionOptions.text: State officials, GJM and Adivasi Vikas Parishad representatives hold joint consultations to narrow the mouza list.

risk.badOutcome: The consultations collapse after competing ethnic groups walk out.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to name a timeline for the Sen committee's report.

title: Maoist Politburo Leader Kishenji Killed in Jangalmahal Encounter (2011-11)
description: CRPF and CoBRA forces kill CPI(Maoist) leader Mallojula Koteswara Rao, alias Kishenji, in Burishole forest, West Midnapore, in an operation the government calls a gun battle. Rights groups and Maoist sympathisers allege he was captured and executed.

reactionOptions.text: The state government credits the joint forces operation and says it will accelerate development spending in Jangalmahal now that the Maoist top command is broken.

risk.badOutcome: Villagers and rights groups produce evidence of torture marks on the body, triggering allegations of a fake encounter.

reactionOptions.text: Left-affiliated rights groups demand an independent probe into whether Kishenji was killed after capture during ongoing peace talks.

risk.badOutcome: The demand is dismissed by security officials as sympathy for a banned terrorist organisation.

reactionOptions.text: State and central interlocutors call for renewed, verifiable peace talks with remaining Maoist cadres to prevent further bloodshed.

risk.badOutcome: Remaining Maoist cadres refuse talks, calling the killing proof that the government negotiated in bad faith.

reactionOptions.text: The chief minister's office declines to detail the exact sequence of events leading to Kishenji's death.

title: Abandoned Dooars Tea Garden Leaves Thousands Without Wages (2011-12)
description: The owner of a large tea estate in the Dooars abruptly shuts operations and leaves the region, stranding thousands of plantation workers without wages just before winter, reviving a recurring crisis in North Bengal's tea belt.

reactionOptions.text: The labour department takes over the garden under the Tea Act and releases emergency wage relief to workers.

risk.badOutcome: Bureaucratic delays mean the promised relief takes weeks to actually reach workers' hands.

reactionOptions.text: Left-affiliated tea workers' unions organise a road blockade demanding the state prosecute the absconding owner for wage theft.

risk.badOutcome: The blockade disrupts supply routes and draws criticism from other tea gardens still operating normally.

reactionOptions.text: All parties back a joint legislative push for a permanent wage-security fund covering abandoned tea estates statewide.

risk.badOutcome: Tea estate owners' associations lobby hard against the proposed fund, slowing its passage.

reactionOptions.text: The labour department offers no immediate timeline for when wages will be disbursed.

title: Calcutta High Court Hears Tata Motors' Challenge to Singur Act (2012-01)
description: Tata Motors moves the Calcutta High Court against the Singur Land Rehabilitation and Development Act, arguing the state's seizure of the Nano plant land violates its contractual rights, setting up a years-long legal battle over the flagship land-return decision.

reactionOptions.text: The state's advocate general defends the Singur Act in court, arguing the legislature has full power to acquire land for redistribution to unwilling farmers.

risk.badOutcome: Legal experts warn the Act's drafting has vulnerabilities that could see it struck down.

reactionOptions.text: Opposition leaders say the legal battle proves the Singur land return was announced without proper legal groundwork.

risk.badOutcome: The criticism rings hollow given the Left's own record of forcible acquisition in Singur.

reactionOptions.text: Legal experts from across party lines are invited to a legislative consultation on strengthening the state's land acquisition framework.

risk.badOutcome: The consultation produces recommendations too late to affect the ongoing case.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment further while the matter is sub judice.

title: Park Street Gang-Rape Sparks Outrage After CM's 'Concocted' Remark (2012-02)
description: A woman is gang-raped in a moving car near Park Street, Kolkata; when she comes forward, Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee publicly calls the case 'concocted,' triggering nationwide condemnation and a debate over the state's handling of crimes against women.

reactionOptions.text: Kolkata Police forms a special team that swiftly identifies and arrests three of the five accused within days.

risk.badOutcome: The chief minister's own dismissal of the case as 'concocted' undercuts the police's credible investigative work.

reactionOptions.text: Left and civil society groups organise a torchlight protest march demanding the chief minister retract her remark and apologise to the survivor.

risk.badOutcome: Our party supporters brand the marchers as politically motivated opportunists rather than genuine advocates for the survivor.

reactionOptions.text: Women's groups across party lines jointly petition the state to set up a fast-track court for the case.

risk.badOutcome: The fast-track court still takes over a year to even frame charges.

reactionOptions.text: The chief minister's office declines to walk back or clarify her 'concocted story' remark.

title: Railway Fare Hike Row Forces Trivedi's Ouster as Rail Minister (2012-03)
description: TMC's Dinesh Trivedi presents a Union Railway Budget with passenger fare hikes; Mamata Banerjee publicly disowns the move as anti-people and forces his resignation days later, replacing him with the more pliant Mukul Roy.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee overrules her own party's railway minister and has the fare hikes substantially rolled back within the week.

risk.badOutcome: The public reversal embarrasses the UPA government and exposes friction inside the our party-opposition coalition.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) MPs mock the episode in Parliament as proof that our party treats national ministries as extensions of Kolkata politics.

risk.badOutcome: The jibe gets less traction once commuters welcome the fare rollback regardless of the politics.

reactionOptions.text: A cross-party parliamentary panel is set up to review railway pricing policy more durably.

risk.badOutcome: The panel's eventual report is quietly shelved.

reactionOptions.text: Dinesh Trivedi declines to publicly criticise his own removal as railway minister.

title: Jadavpur Professor Arrested Over Mamata Cartoon Email (2012-04)
description: Police arrest Jadavpur University chemistry professor Ambikesh Mahapatra for forwarding an email containing a cartoon of Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, drawing nationwide criticism of the new government's tolerance for dissent and satire.

reactionOptions.text: Kolkata Police defends the arrest, citing a complaint of criminal defamation and obscenity filed by a local our party councillor.

risk.badOutcome: National editorials and cartoonists' bodies condemn the arrest as an attack on free speech, badly denting the government's image.

reactionOptions.text: Civil liberties groups and opposition leaders demand Mahapatra's immediate release and repeal of the case against him.

risk.badOutcome: Our party dismisses the outcry as CPI(M) nostalgia for its own record of suppressing dissent.

reactionOptions.text: Academics across party lines petition for the withdrawal of the case and a review of how the IT Act is being used against satire.

risk.badOutcome: The state is slow to act on the petition, keeping the case in limbo for months.

reactionOptions.text: The chief minister's office refuses to answer questions on why the cartoon warranted a police complaint.

title: State Unveils Jangalmahal Package to Wean Youth from Maoist Ranks (2012-05)
description: The state government announces a development and jobs package for the Jangalmahal belt, including skill-training centres and infrastructure funds, aimed at consolidating peace in the region following Kishenji's death.

reactionOptions.text: Fast-track road and electrification projects in Jangalmahal villages and opens new skill-training centres for tribal youth.

risk.badOutcome: Contractors delay several projects, and villagers complain the promised jobs are slow to materialise.

reactionOptions.text: Left-affiliated tribal rights groups say the package ignores land rights and forest-dweller claims that predate the Maoist insurgency.

risk.badOutcome: The criticism is dismissed by officials as reflexive opposition rather than a substantive alternative.

reactionOptions.text: A joint monitoring committee with local representatives is set up to track the package's implementation transparently.

risk.badOutcome: The committee's early meetings are poorly attended by district officials.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to give a firm timeline for project completion.

title: Mamata Floats Alternative Names as Congress Pushes Pranab for President (2012-06)
description: As the Congress-led UPA moves to nominate Pranab Mukherjee for President, Mamata Banerjee publicly proposes alternative names including APJ Abdul Kalam, straining her alliance with the Congress just months after the railway budget standoff.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee holds a press conference proposing a shortlist of consensus candidates and insists our party's support cannot be taken for granted.

risk.badOutcome: The move is read in Delhi as brinkmanship, further straining ties with the opposition-led coalition.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) mocks the episode as proof our party's national ambitions outstrip its actual bargaining power within the UPA.

risk.badOutcome: The jibe lands weakly since the Left itself has no real say in the presidential nomination.

reactionOptions.text: Regional parties across the political spectrum hold informal talks on a genuinely consensual presidential nominee.

risk.badOutcome: The talks collapse once the opposition makes clear it will not budge from its chosen candidate.

reactionOptions.text: Our party's central leadership declines to confirm whether it will ultimately back Pranab Mukherjee.

title: Bengal's Pranab Mukherjee Elected President of India (2012-07)
description: Pranab Mukherjee, the veteran Congress leader and Bengal's own political export, is elected President of India, with the Trinamool Congress ultimately extending its support despite earlier reservations, easing tensions within the ruling coalition.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee congratulates Mukherjee and frames the state's eventual support as evidence of our party's statesmanship over petty politics.

risk.badOutcome: Critics note our party's reversal from its earlier objections looks more like a retreat than a principled stand.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) claims credit for having always supported a candidate of Mukherjee's stature, distancing itself from our party's earlier hesitation.

risk.badOutcome: The claim is largely ignored given the Left's limited numbers in the electoral college.

reactionOptions.text: Bengal's political class jointly celebrates a home-state leader reaching Rashtrapati Bhavan, briefly setting aside partisan sniping.

risk.badOutcome: The bonhomie proves short-lived as normal political hostilities resume within days.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment on a result it had no realistic path to influence.

title: GJM Sweeps GTA Polls, New Hill Council Sworn In at Darjeeling (2012-08)
description: The Gorkha Janmukti Morcha wins all 45 seats of the newly formed Gorkhaland Territorial Administration, with elected members sworn in at Darjeeling in the presence of Union Home Minister Sushilkumar Shinde and Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee attends the swearing-in personally and pledges expedited fund transfers to the new GTA administration.

risk.badOutcome: Delays in the promised fund transfers soon frustrate the newly elected GTA members.

reactionOptions.text: GJM leaders use the ceremony to reiterate that GTA is a stepping stone, not a substitute, for full statehood.

risk.badOutcome: The renewed statehood rhetoric worries non-Gorkha residents of the plains adjoining the hills.

reactionOptions.text: Union and state officials jointly commit to a phased fund-devolution schedule to give the new council early credibility.

risk.badOutcome: The devolution schedule is only partially honoured in its first year.

reactionOptions.text: The CPI(M), long shut out of hill politics, declines to comment on the GJM's uncontested sweep.

title: Trinamool Congress Withdraws Support From UPA Over FDI in Retail (2012-09)
description: Mamata Banerjee pulls the Trinamool Congress out of the UPA government at the Centre, protesting the decision to allow foreign direct investment in multi-brand retail, ending her ministers' tenure in New Delhi and reshaping national coalition arithmetic.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee announces our party's ministers will resign from the Union cabinet and campaigns statewide against FDI's impact on small traders.

risk.badOutcome: The abrupt exit leaves West Bengal's bargaining leverage with the Centre for funds and projects considerably weaker.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) calls the move a belated and self-serving reaction, noting the party had long warned against FDI liberalisation.

risk.badOutcome: The Left's own criticism is diluted since it too now technically shares our party's anti-FDI stance.

reactionOptions.text: Regional parties opposed to FDI in retail hold a joint press conference presenting a united front against the policy.

risk.badOutcome: The show of unity fades once individual parties' other political interests diverge.

reactionOptions.text: The opposition high command declines to immediately respond to Banerjee's withdrawal announcement.

title: Trinamool Holds Mass Brigade Rally Against FDI in Retail (2012-10)
description: Mamata Banerjee addresses a massive rally at Kolkata's Brigade Parade Ground, warning that foreign supermarket chains will devastate small traders and hawkers, cementing her party's newly independent, anti-Congress national posture after quitting the UPA.

reactionOptions.text: Announce a hawkers' protection policy alongside the rally, promising no forced evictions of street vendors.

risk.badOutcome: Traders' groups later complain the promised protections were never formally notified.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) organises a smaller counter-rally accusing our party of stealing the Left's traditional anti-liberalisation plank for electoral gain.

risk.badOutcome: The counter-rally draws a fraction of the crowd, underscoring the Left's diminished mobilising power.

reactionOptions.text: Traders' associations across party lines jointly submit a memorandum requesting statutory protection from big-box retail.

risk.badOutcome: The memorandum makes little legislative progress in the following months.

reactionOptions.text: The opposition state unit declines to join or comment on the rally against its own central government's policy.

title: Coal Block Scam Uproar in Parliament Reaches Bengal's Left Benches (2012-11)
description: Winter session proceedings in Parliament are repeatedly stalled over the CAG's coal block allocation report, with West Bengal's CPI(M) MPs using the scandal to attack both the Congress-led Centre and, indirectly, Trinamool's earlier coalition partnership with it.

reactionOptions.text: State our party leaders distance the party from the scam, noting they had already quit the UPA before the report's fallout peaked.

risk.badOutcome: Critics note our party ministers held Union portfolios for over a year while coal block allocations were finalised.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) MPs demand a joint parliamentary committee probe and use West Bengal rallies to link the scam to 'opposition-our party crony politics'.

risk.badOutcome: The attack line struggles to land since CPI(M) itself governed with opposition support for years at the Centre.

reactionOptions.text: Bengal's MPs across parties jointly push for greater transparency in future coal and mineral block allocations.

risk.badOutcome: The push has little practical effect since block allocation policy is set at the Centre.

reactionOptions.text: Our party's central leadership declines to detail its own role while it was part of the UPA cabinet.

title: RBI Governor Warns Bengal to Act on Chit Fund Malpractice (2012-12)
description: RBI Governor Duvvuri Subbarao publicly urges the West Bengal government to take suo motu action against companies engaged in financial malpractice, an early warning about the very Ponzi-style collective investment schemes that will soon collapse into the Saradha scandal.

reactionOptions.text: The state finance department says it will examine unregulated deposit-taking firms but stops short of naming any specific company for action.

risk.badOutcome: The vague response leaves large chit-fund-style schemes like Saradha entirely unchecked in the following months.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) MPs demand the state name and investigate specific collective investment schemes operating with political patronage.

risk.badOutcome: Our party dismisses the demand as an attempt to smear legitimate rural savings cooperatives.

reactionOptions.text: An all-party assembly committee is proposed to draft stronger deposit-taking regulation for the state.

risk.badOutcome: The proposal is not acted on before the schemes it targets begin to collapse anyway.

reactionOptions.text: The state government declines to specify which companies, if any, are under scrutiny.

title: Saradha Group's Payouts Begin Outpacing New Deposits (2013-01)
description: Agents for the Saradha Group quietly report that payouts to existing depositors are for the first time exceeding fresh collections, an internal warning sign of a collapsing Ponzi scheme that regulators and the state government have yet to act on.

reactionOptions.text: The state government asks its Economic Offences Wing to quietly assess the finances of large collective investment firms operating in Bengal.

risk.badOutcome: The assessment moves too slowly to catch the scheme before it collapses on ordinary depositors.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) legislators raise the payout slowdown in the assembly, demanding the government name which chit-fund-style firms are under watch.

risk.badOutcome: The government brushes off the question as unsubstantiated rumour-mongering.

reactionOptions.text: An all-party assembly panel calls for an urgent joint audit of collective investment schemes before the situation worsens.

risk.badOutcome: The audit proposal is tabled but not acted upon before the group's April collapse.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment on any specific company's cash flow.

title: Fast-Track Court Frames Gang-Rape Charges in Park Street Case (2013-02)
description: A year after the incident, a fast-track court in Kolkata formally frames charges of gang-rape, criminal intimidation and conspiracy against three accused in the Park Street case, marking slow but tangible judicial progress after months of political controversy.

reactionOptions.text: The state prosecution welcomes the charge-framing and pledges a time-bound trial through the fast-track court mechanism.

risk.badOutcome: Defence lawyers signal they will seek repeated adjournments, threatening the promised timeline.

reactionOptions.text: Women's rights groups say the year-long delay in framing charges shows the need for permanent, not case-specific, fast-track courts.

risk.badOutcome: The state government resists committing to a permanent fast-track court network, citing cost.

reactionOptions.text: Legal aid groups across party lines jointly push for victim support services to be strengthened for the remainder of the trial.

risk.badOutcome: Support services remain patchy outside major cities despite the push.

reactionOptions.text: The chief minister's office again declines to revisit her earlier 'concocted story' remark now that charges have been framed.

title: Saradha Ponzi Scheme Raised in Lok Sabha by Union Minister Sachin Pilot (2013-03)
description: Union minister Sachin Pilot flags the Saradha Group's Ponzi-style operations on the floor of the Lok Sabha, pushing the simmering West Bengal financial scandal onto the national stage weeks before the group's eventual collapse.

reactionOptions.text: West Bengal's finance department issues a statement insisting existing regulations are adequate and that no company has broken the law.

risk.badOutcome: The reassurance ages poorly within weeks as the scheme publicly collapses.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) MPs demand the Centre order an immediate SEBI investigation into Saradha's collective investment schemes.

risk.badOutcome: The Centre is slow to act, with SEBI's jurisdictional powers over such schemes still contested.

reactionOptions.text: Parliament's finance standing committee agrees to examine gaps in regulating unlisted collective investment schemes nationally.

risk.badOutcome: The committee's review is overtaken by events before it can report.

reactionOptions.text: The state government declines to respond directly to Pilot's remarks in Parliament.

title: Saradha Group Collapses; Chairman Sudipto Sen Arrested in Kashmir (2013-04)
description: The Saradha Group's Ponzi scheme collapses after Sudipto Sen writes an 18-page confessional letter to the CBI naming politicians he says received payments; he is arrested days later in Sonmarg, Kashmir, along with two associates, triggering a full-blown political crisis.

reactionOptions.text: Chief Minister Banerjee announces a Special Investigation Team and a state relief fund for depositors within days of the collapse.

risk.badOutcome: Sen's confessional letter names our party-linked figures directly, undercutting the government's damage-control effort.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) demands a CBI probe rather than a state-run SIT, arguing the ruling party cannot credibly investigate its own leaders.

risk.badOutcome: The demand is dismissed by the state as an attempt to drag the Centre into a state matter.

reactionOptions.text: Legislators across party lines back a fast-tracked depositor compensation bill to shield the poorest victims first.

risk.badOutcome: The compensation fund proves too small to cover the scale of losses across the state.

reactionOptions.text: Several named our party leaders decline to respond to Sen's allegations pending the SIT's findings.

title: Odisha Police Seize Saradha Documents as Probe Widens Beyond Bengal (2013-05)
description: Odisha police raid and seal Saradha Group offices, seizing documents as thousands of complaints pour in from depositors outside West Bengal, while the state government resists central pressure to hand the multi-state probe to the CBI.

reactionOptions.text: West Bengal's SIT insists it is coordinating with Odisha, Assam and Tripura police to keep the investigation within state-level control.

risk.badOutcome: Other states' independent action makes the state's insistence on control look increasingly untenable.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) and other states' ruling parties jointly press the Supreme Court to transfer the entire multi-state probe to the CBI.

risk.badOutcome: The state government's legal team resists the transfer plea in court for over a year.

reactionOptions.text: Officials from the affected states hold a coordination meeting to share evidence and prevent suspects from fleeing across state lines.

risk.badOutcome: Coordination remains patchy given each state's separate legal proceedings.

reactionOptions.text: Odisha's Economic Offences Wing declines to share details of what its seized documents reveal.

title: Kamduni Gang-Rape and Murder Sparks Statewide Protests (2013-06)
description: The gang-rape and murder of a young woman in Kamduni, Barasat, ignites statewide protests demanding justice; when local women confront Chief Minister Banerjee, she accuses them of playing 'CPM politics,' deepening public anger over the government's response to crimes against women.

reactionOptions.text: Police make swift arrests of the accused and the state announces additional women's safety patrols in North 24 Parganas.

risk.badOutcome: The chief minister's dismissal of protesting local women as playing politics reignites the same backlash seen after Park Street.

reactionOptions.text: Opposition parties and civil society groups back the Kamduni women's protest, demanding the chief minister retract her remark and meet the victim's family.

risk.badOutcome: Our party loyalists accuse the opposition of using a grieving village for a media spectacle.

reactionOptions.text: Women's safety groups across party lines jointly demand a statewide review of rural policing and street lighting in isolated areas.

risk.badOutcome: The review is announced but implementation is patchy outside high-profile districts.

reactionOptions.text: The chief minister's office declines to walk back the 'CPM politics' remark despite mounting criticism.

title: Panchayat Elections Marred by Violence Across Rural Bengal (2013-07)
description: West Bengal holds three-tier panchayat elections marked by widespread clashes between TMC and opposition workers, with dozens killed in the run-up to and on polling day, even as the ruling party sweeps the vast majority of seats.

reactionOptions.text: Deploy additional police for the remaining polling phases and orders an inquiry into the worst-hit constituencies.

risk.badOutcome: Independent observers say the deployment came too late to prevent much of the violence.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) and opposition jointly demand central forces be deployed for all remaining phases and call the state election commission complicit in the bloodshed.

risk.badOutcome: The state government resists central force deployment, citing constitutional prerogative over state elections.

reactionOptions.text: All parties agree, under Calcutta High Court pressure, to an enhanced central and state force deployment for subsequent phases.

risk.badOutcome: Even the enhanced deployment cannot fully prevent further clashes in remote booths.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to give a running death toll as the violence continues.

title: Parliament Amends SEBI Act, Giving Regulator Search-and-Seizure Powers (2013-08)
description: In direct response to the Saradha fallout, Parliament amends the SEBI Act to grant the regulator powers to search and seize records without prior magisterial permission when investigating illegal money-collection schemes across states.

reactionOptions.text: The state government says the amended SEBI Act will help close the regulatory gaps that allowed Saradha-style schemes to flourish.

risk.badOutcome: Critics note the amendment comes only after the damage from Saradha's collapse was already done.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) MPs argue the amendment should have come years earlier when RBI first flagged the risk in 2012.

risk.badOutcome: The retrospective criticism gains little new traction once the law has already changed.

reactionOptions.text: Bengal's MPs across party lines jointly back the SEBI Act amendment's passage in Parliament without partisan wrangling.

risk.badOutcome: Implementation of the new powers on the ground still takes months to operationalise.

reactionOptions.text: SEBI officials decline to comment on how many active investigations the new powers will immediately affect.

title: State Sets Up Rs 500 Crore Fund for Small Saradha Depositors (2013-09)
description: The West Bengal government creates a special welfare fund of around Rs 500 crore to compensate low-income Saradha depositors, an unusual step to use public money to cushion victims of a private Ponzi scheme amid mounting political pressure.

reactionOptions.text: Chief Minister Banerjee announces the relief fund personally, framing it as the state standing by ordinary depositors regardless of who is to blame.

risk.badOutcome: Reports later surface of cheques from the fund bouncing for a significant number of claimants.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) calls the fund an admission of political guilt and demands the money instead be recovered from the auctioned assets of accused politicians.

risk.badOutcome: The demand for asset recovery makes little headway given ongoing court proceedings.

reactionOptions.text: An all-party oversight committee is proposed to ensure the relief fund's disbursement is transparent and reaches genuine small depositors.

risk.badOutcome: The committee finds disbursement records incomplete in several districts.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to specify how the relief fund is being financed.

title: State Launches Kanyashree Prakalpo Scholarship Scheme for Girls (2013-10)
description: The West Bengal government launches Kanyashree Prakalpo, a scholarship and conditional cash-transfer scheme to keep adolescent girls in school and delay early marriage, positioning it as a signature welfare achievement amid the ongoing Saradha turmoil.

reactionOptions.text: Chief Minister Banerjee launches Kanyashree Prakalpo in a large public event, presenting it as proof her government delivers welfare even amid scandal.

risk.badOutcome: Implementation gaps mean some eligible girls in remote districts are left out in the scheme's first months.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) welcomes the scheme's intent but demands independent audits given the government's recent record on public fund disbursement.

risk.badOutcome: The audit demand is seen by some as churlish given the scheme's broad popularity.

reactionOptions.text: Education and women's welfare groups across party lines jointly back expanding Kanyashree's eligibility criteria over time.

risk.badOutcome: Expansion plans are deferred to a future budget cycle.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to give exact enrolment figures at launch.

title: TMC MP Kunal Ghosh Arrested, Implicates Senior Leaders in Saradha Probe (2013-11)
description: Trinamool Rajya Sabha MP Kunal Ghosh, a former media executive linked to Saradha's television ventures, is arrested and makes explosive statements to investigators implicating senior party leaders, deepening the scandal's reach into the ruling party's top ranks.

reactionOptions.text: The party suspends Ghosh's primary membership and insists his allegations are the desperate claims of a man facing prosecution.

risk.badOutcome: Ghosh's detailed statements to the SIT keep generating fresh headlines the party cannot control.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) demands every leader named by Ghosh be investigated without exception, regardless of rank within the ruling party.

risk.badOutcome: The party in power resists broadening the probe, calling Ghosh's claims unverified.

reactionOptions.text: Legal experts across party lines call for the SIT's findings on Ghosh's claims to be made public in a time-bound manner.

risk.badOutcome: The findings are not released before the case is eventually transferred to the CBI.

reactionOptions.text: Several leaders named by Ghosh decline to respond to his allegations directly.

title: State Secretariat Formally Shifts to New Nabanna Building in Howrah (2013-12)
description: The West Bengal government completes its move from the century-old Writers' Building to the new Nabanna complex across the Hooghly in Howrah, ending an era of colonial-vintage administration even as the Saradha scandal continues to dominate headlines.

reactionOptions.text: Chief Minister Banerjee inaugurates Nabanna as a symbol of modern, efficient administration distinct from the our coalition era's Writers' Building.

risk.badOutcome: Critics note the costly relocation comes at an odd time given the ongoing scam-related distractions.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) questions the cost and timing of the shift, saying public funds would be better spent on scam-hit depositors.

risk.badOutcome: The criticism struggles to resonate once Nabanna becomes functionally accepted as the new seat of government.

reactionOptions.text: Heritage conservationists across party lines welcome plans to preserve Writers' Building as a protected monument after the move.

risk.badOutcome: Conservation funding for Writers' Building remains uncertain in subsequent years.

reactionOptions.text: The public works department declines to detail the total cost of the Nabanna relocation.

title: SIT Files Wave of New FIRs as Saradha Probe Widens Across Districts (2014-01)
description: The state's Special Investigation Team files a fresh wave of FIRs against Saradha-linked companies and agents across multiple districts, pushing the total case count toward several hundred as the probe's scale becomes clearer nearly a year after the collapse.

reactionOptions.text: The SIT publicises the growing FIR count as evidence the state-led probe is making real progress without central interference.

risk.badOutcome: Depositors note that FIRs rarely translate into recovered money, deepening frustration with the pace of justice.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) argues the sheer number of FIRs shows the scale is too large for a state police-led SIT and again demands a CBI takeover.

risk.badOutcome: The government continues resisting a CBI handover, citing ongoing court proceedings.

reactionOptions.text: An all-party legislative panel calls for a public dashboard tracking FIR status and depositor compensation progress.

risk.badOutcome: The dashboard proposal is not implemented before the case is transferred to the CBI later in the year.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment on how many of the FIRs have led to actual convictions so far.

title: Sudipto Sen Gets First Conviction, Jailed for Provident Fund Default (2014-02)
description: Saradha Group chairman Sudipto Sen is convicted and sentenced to three years in jail for failing to deposit employees' provident fund dues, his first conviction in what will become a long series of civil and criminal cases arising from the scandal.

reactionOptions.text: The state prosecution cites the conviction as proof that due legal process, however slow, is being followed against those responsible.

risk.badOutcome: Critics note this first conviction addresses only a minor labour-law violation, not the core fraud allegations.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) calls the conviction a token gesture that avoids the far larger question of political complicity in the scam.

risk.badOutcome: The criticism is echoed by many depositors who see little connection between this case and their lost savings.

reactionOptions.text: Legal aid groups across party lines push for the larger fraud cases against Sen to be expedited using the same court infrastructure.

risk.badOutcome: The larger fraud cases remain pending well beyond this first, minor conviction.

reactionOptions.text: Sen's legal team declines to comment on the provident fund conviction while other cases remain pending.

title: Trinamool Announces It Will Contest All 42 Lok Sabha Seats Alone (2014-03)
description: For the first time, the Trinamool Congress announces it will contest every one of West Bengal's 42 Lok Sabha seats without an alliance with either the Congress or the BJP, launching a solo campaign built around Mamata Banerjee's personal appeal.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee kicks off a statewide rally circuit, betting her personal popularity can overcome the drag of the Saradha scandal.

risk.badOutcome: Opposition parties seize on the scandal at every rally stop, forcing Banerjee onto the defensive repeatedly.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) and opposition independently launch their own campaigns, betting a divided anti-our party vote is preferable to a compromised alliance.

risk.badOutcome: Splitting the opposition vote across three-cornered contests risks handing our party an easier path to most seats.

reactionOptions.text: The Election Commission holds an all-party meeting to set ground rules for a campaign expected to be unusually combative.

risk.badOutcome: The ground rules do little to curb the aggressive tone that follows in subsequent weeks.

reactionOptions.text: The opposition's state unit, still building its Bengal organisation, declines to comment on our party's solo strategy.

title: Supreme Court Signals It May Order CBI Takeover of Ponzi Scheme Probes (2014-04)
description: A Supreme Court bench hearing petitions on the Saradha and related Ponzi schemes indicates it may transfer investigations across West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and other states to the CBI, alarming a state government that has resisted central involvement for a year.

title: Trinamool Sweeps Bengal in Lok Sabha Polls as Left Collapses to Two Seats (2014-05)

reactionOptions.text: The opposition's state unit declines to claim victory despite its best-ever vote share, given its modest seat count.

title: CBI Formally Takes Custody of Saradha Accused From State SIT (2014-06)
description: Acting on the Supreme Court's May order, the CBI formally takes over the Saradha investigation, assuming custody of Sudipto Sen, Debjani Mukherjee and Kunal Ghosh from the state SIT, ending a year of the state government's resistance to central involvement.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) says the transfer vindicates a year of demands and calls for the CBI to also examine why the state SIT moved so slowly on senior leaders.

risk.badOutcome: The state government pushes back hard against any suggestion its SIT deliberately slow-walked the case.

reactionOptions.text: Legal experts across party lines call for a transparent, time-bound CBI chargesheet process given the scale of public interest.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment on the handover of evidence and custody to the CBI.

title: Left Front Begins Painful Introspection After Worst-Ever Poll Result (2014-07)
description: Following its collapse to just two Lok Sabha seats, the CPI(M)-led Left Front holds state committee meetings to diagnose its organisational decline in rural Bengal, with sharp internal disagreements over whether the party has been too slow to adapt since 2011.

risk.badOutcome: Critics accuse the government of exploiting a rival's organisational weakness rather than governing on its own merits.

reactionOptions.text: Younger opposition leaders publicly demand a generational change in the state leadership to reconnect with rural voters.

risk.badOutcome: The demand triggers open factional friction with the party's old guard.

reactionOptions.text: Political analysts across affiliations are invited to a public seminar on the Left's decline and Bengal's shifting party system.

risk.badOutcome: The seminar's diagnosis has little immediate effect on the party's actual organisational practice.

reactionOptions.text: The CPI(M) state secretariat declines to detail specifics of its internal review.

title: CBI Questions Former DGP Rajat Majumdar in Saradha Probe (2014-08)
description: The CBI questions Rajat Majumdar, a former Director General of Police who went on to become a Trinamool Congress vice-president, over his alleged links to the Saradha Group, drawing the scandal further into the state's security establishment.

risk.badOutcome: The involvement of a former top police officer intensifies public perception of institutional capture by the scandal.

reactionOptions.text: Retired civil servants across party lines call for a review of post-retirement political appointments for former top officials.

reactionOptions.text: Majumdar's office declines to comment while the CBI's questioning is ongoing.

title: Another Dooars Tea Estate Shuts Down, Reviving Wage-Crisis Fears (2014-09)
description: A second major Dooars tea estate abruptly halts operations and its owner disappears, leaving workers without wages ahead of the Puja season and reviving memories of the 2011 plantation crisis that the state's tea-belt relief mechanisms have still not fully resolved.

risk.badOutcome: Estate owners' associations again lobby against a mandatory trust fund, slowing the proposal.

reactionOptions.text: The labour department declines to say why the 2011 relief mechanism failed to prevent a repeat crisis.

title: Accidental Blast at Burdwan House Exposes JMB Terror Module (2014-10)
description: An improvised explosive device detonates accidentally inside a rented house in Khagragarh, Burdwan, killing two men and exposing a Jamaat-ul-Mujahideen Bangladesh module allegedly plotting attacks in Kolkata during Durga Puja, prompting a swift National Investigation Agency takeover of the case.

reactionOptions.text: State police hand the case to the NIA within days and launch a statewide crackdown on suspected cross-border terror modules.

risk.badOutcome: Opposition parties allege the state government had been slow to act on earlier intelligence warnings about such modules operating in border districts.

reactionOptions.text: The opposition demands a full accounting of how a bomb-making module operated undetected for months, calling it a serious border security failure.

reactionOptions.text: Central and state agencies jointly agree to strengthen intelligence-sharing along the West Bengal-Bangladesh border districts.

risk.badOutcome: Coordination gaps between state police and central agencies persist despite the agreement.

reactionOptions.text: The state home department declines to detail what prior intelligence, if any, existed on the Khagragarh module.

title: CBI Arrests TMC Rajya Sabha MP Srinjoy Bose in Saradha Case (2014-11)
description: The CBI arrests Trinamool Rajya Sabha member Srinjoy Bose, a media entrepreneur with business ties to the Saradha Group, marking the second sitting TMC parliamentarian taken into custody in the scandal within a year.

reactionOptions.text: The party again suspends the arrested MP's primary membership pending the outcome of the case, distancing itself organisationally.

risk.badOutcome: A second sitting MP's arrest within a year deepens public perception that the scandal reaches the party's core, not its fringes.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) and opposition jointly demand the chief minister explain how two of her own Rajya Sabha MPs ended up facing arrest in the same case.

title: CBI Arrests Transport Minister Madan Mitra in Saradha Case (2014-12)
description: The CBI arrests sitting West Bengal transport minister Madan Mitra on charges of criminal conspiracy and cheating linked to the Saradha Group, marking the first arrest of a serving state cabinet minister in the scandal and capping a year of escalating action against the ruling party's leadership.

risk.badOutcome: The first-ever arrest of a sitting minister in the scandal severely damages the government's credibility heading into 2015.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) and opposition jointly demand the chief minister's resignation, arguing a minister's arrest proves complicity reaches the cabinet table itself.

risk.badOutcome: The resignation demand is dismissed by the ruling party as an overreach unsupported by any charge against the chief minister personally.

reactionOptions.text: Legal and civil society groups across party lines call for an expedited, transparent trial given Mitra's cabinet rank.

risk.badOutcome: The trial nonetheless proceeds slowly, mirroring the broader pace of the multi-year Saradha case.

reactionOptions.text: Decline to comment on Mitra's arrest beyond confirming his removal from ministerial duties.

title: CBI Questions TMC Heavyweight Mukul Roy in Saradha Case (2015-01)
description: The CBI questions senior Trinamool leader and Rajya Sabha MP Mukul Roy over his links to the Saradha Group, a session that marks the start of a lasting rift between Roy and Chief Minister Banerjee even as the party publicly insists he remains a valued leader.

reactionOptions.text: The party publicly stands by Roy, with the chief minister's office insisting the questioning does not imply any wrongdoing.

risk.badOutcome: Behind closed doors, the questioning triggers lasting suspicion between Roy and the party leadership that will fester for years.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) says the questioning of yet another top our party leader shows the scam's roots reach the party's original founding circle.

risk.badOutcome: The party in power dismisses the claim as recycled rhetoric with nothing new to show.

reactionOptions.text: Legal observers across party lines call for the CBI to clarify whether Roy is a witness or a suspect to reduce public speculation.

risk.badOutcome: The CBI declines to clarify Roy's exact status, keeping the ambiguity alive for months.

reactionOptions.text: Mukul Roy declines to comment on the substance of his questioning by the CBI.

title: Trinamool Opposes Centre's Land Bill, Invokes Singur-Nandigram Legacy (2015-02)
description: As the Centre pushes its Land Acquisition Amendment Bill diluting the consent clause for land takeovers, Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress joins opposition parties in the Rajya Sabha to block it, drawing on the same Singur and Nandigram land-rights history that first brought her to power.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee publicly frames our party's Rajya Sabha opposition as consistent with the farmer-first politics that ended our coalition rule.

risk.badOutcome: Critics note her own government continues to acquire land for industrial projects using different legal routes.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) says it welcomes our party's opposition to the bill but insists the Left's own historical land-reform record is the real template for protecting farmers.

risk.badOutcome: The competing claims to farmer-friendly credentials produce more point-scoring than substantive policy debate.

reactionOptions.text: Bengal's MPs across parties jointly caucus in the Rajya Sabha to coordinate a unified rejection of the consent-clause dilution.

risk.badOutcome: The unified stand does not extend to agreement on what a state-level alternative should look like.

reactionOptions.text: The state's industry department declines to say how future land acquisition for projects will proceed if the bill is blocked.

title: Rose Valley Chairman Gautam Kundu Arrested in Scam Bigger Than Saradha (2015-03)
description: The CBI arrests Rose Valley Group chairman Gautam Kundu over an alleged Ponzi scheme worth more than Rs 15,000 crore, exposing a second major chit-fund collapse with deep ties to Bengal's film industry, sports sponsorships and television channels, and renewed questions about political patronage.

reactionOptions.text: The state government says it will extend the same category of depositor-protection measures used for Saradha victims to Rose Valley's depositors.

risk.badOutcome: Unlike with Saradha, no dedicated state relief fund materialises for Rose Valley's far larger depositor base.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) and opposition jointly demand to know why a scheme seven times the size of Saradha was allowed to operate for years despite a 2009 SEBI warning.

risk.badOutcome: The government insists SEBI's own regulatory gaps, not state inaction, are chiefly to blame.

reactionOptions.text: Legislators across party lines push for a joint legislative audit covering all major chit-fund-style companies operating in the state, not just the two already exposed.

risk.badOutcome: The audit proposal stalls amid disagreement over which agency should lead it.

reactionOptions.text: Rose Valley's remaining corporate leadership declines to comment on Kundu's arrest.

title: Trinamool Sweeps Kolkata and Civic Body Polls Despite Scam Allegations (2015-04)
description: The Trinamool Congress wins a landslide 114 of 144 Kolkata Municipal Corporation seats and most of the state's other civic bodies, with Mamata Banerjee calling the result a rebuttal to opposition attacks over the Saradha and Rose Valley scandals.

reactionOptions.text: Banerjee declares the result a public vote of confidence and reshuffles the Kolkata mayoral team to project a fresh, scandal-distanced face.

risk.badOutcome: Opposition parties allege large-scale rigging and intimidation in several wards, denting the credibility of the win.

reactionOptions.text: CPI(M) and opposition allege widespread rigging and demand a probe into voting irregularities in dozens of contested wards.

risk.badOutcome: The state election commission finds insufficient evidence to order repolling in most disputed wards.

reactionOptions.text: Civil society election-monitoring groups across affiliations call for stronger CCTV coverage of polling booths in future civic polls.

risk.badOutcome: The proposal is noted but not implemented in time for the very next round of local body polls.

title: Parliament Passes 100th Amendment Enabling India-Bangladesh Enclave Swap (2015-05)

reactionOptions.text: Chief Minister Banerjee, once a skeptic of ceding any Bengal territory, publicly backs the amendment after securing assurances on compensation and rehabilitation for affected residents.

risk.badOutcome: Some Cooch Behar residents remain uneasy about the practicalities of choosing citizenship and leaving ancestral land.

reactionOptions.text: Left MPs, who first pushed the enclave issue for decades, say the amendment vindicates years of parliamentary advocacy that predates the current government.

risk.badOutcome: Our party disputes the Left's claim to primary credit for the amendment's final passage.

reactionOptions.text: MPs across every party represented from Bengal vote together for the amendment, a rare moment of unanimity in the state's fractious politics.

risk.badOutcome: The unanimity in Parliament does not fully carry over into agreement on implementation details back home.

reactionOptions.text: The state home department declines to detail rehabilitation plans for enclave residents pending the treaty's formal implementation.

title: Modi Signs Land Boundary Instruments in Dhaka, Mamata Banerjee Attends (2015-06)
description: Prime Minister Modi visits Dhaka and formally signs the instruments implementing the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement alongside Sheikh Hasina, with Chief Minister Banerjee attending in a rare display of state-Centre cooperation on an issue with direct implications for North Bengal's border districts.

title: India and Bangladesh Formally Exchange Enclaves at Midnight (2015-07)

title: Monsoon Floods Inundate North Bengal Districts, Displace Thousands (2015-08)
description: Heavy monsoon rains swell rivers across Jalpaiguri, Cooch Behar and the Dooars, breaching embankments and displacing thousands of families, testing the state's disaster response machinery even as reconstruction from the previous year's tea-garden crises remains incomplete.

title: Kolkata Court Convicts Three in Park Street Gang-Rape Case (2015-12)

title: Mamata Refuses to Speak at Modi's Parakram Diwas Event After 'Jai Shri Ram' Chants (2021-01)

title: CBI Summons Abhishek Banerjee's Wife in Coal Smuggling Probe Weeks Before Polls (2021-02)

title: Phase 1 Polling Opens Amid EVM Malfunction Claims and Purba Medinipur Firing (2021-03)

title: CISF Firing Kills Four Voters at Sitalkuchi Booth During Phase 4 Polling (2021-04)

reactionOptions.text: Sanyukta Morcha leaders visit victims' families with representatives from all fronts and jointly demand a judicially monitored, non-partisan inquiry.

title: TMC Wins Historic Third Term as Mamata Loses Nandigram to Suvendu Adhikari (2021-05)

title: Mukul Roy Quits BJP, Returns to TMC Fold Barely a Month After Winning on Its Ticket (2021-06)

title: Calcutta High Court Orders CBI Probe Into Post-Poll Murders and Rapes (2021-08)

title: Mamata Wins Bhabanipur by Record Margin, Returns to the Assembly (2021-10)

title: Kirti Azad and Pavan Varma Join TMC as Party Pushes National Ambitions (2021-11)

title: Kolkata's Durga Puja Wins UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Recognition (2021-12)
